item.title: Open Legacy IE-Only Websites with Microsoft Edge IE Mode
item.description:
Microsoft has retired Internet Explorer and replaced it with Microsoft Edge. Some legacy business websites still require IE-specific behavior, but Edge includes an Internet Explorer compatibility mode that may allow them to run.

I encountered the compatibility prompt while opening Zhongqi Cloud Chain :

Enable Internet Explorer Mode in Microsoft Edge

  1. Open Edge, click the three-dot menu in the upper-right corner, and select Settings.

  2. Select Default browser. Set Allow sites to be reloaded in Internet Explorer mode to Allow.

  3. Click Restart so the setting takes effect.

  4. After Edge restarts, open the required page, open the three-dot menu again, and select Reload in Internet Explorer mode.

item.title: Safely Free Windows Disk Space: Temporary Files, Storage Sense and Cleanup
item.description:
The Windows system drive can gradually lose free space as temporary files, update caches, recycle-bin contents, and application data accumulate.

The original article proposed a batch file that recursively deleted every .tmp, .log, .old, and several other file types across the entire system drive. That approach is too broad: those extensions may contain active application data, diagnostic records, or files required for recovery. A safer process is to use Windows’ built-in cleanup controls.

item.title: Fix Look for an App in Microsoft Store on Windows 11 for a Trusted EXE
item.description:
Problem

When opening an .exe installer on Windows 11, you may see Look for an app in the Microsoft Store?

Solution for a trusted file

Right-click the .exe, select Properties, and open the General tab. If an Unblock checkbox appears in the Security section, select it and click Apply.

Only unblock a file after confirming its source and digital signature and scanning it with Windows Security. If Windows still cannot run it, verify that it is actually a Windows executable for the correct processor architecture rather than bypassing additional warnings.

item.title: macOS App Is Damaged: Verify Source, Signature, Notarization and Quarantine
item.description:
macOS may report that an application “is damaged and can’t be opened” when the download is actually corrupted, the signature is invalid, notarization is missing, or the package has been modified after signing. Treat the warning as a security signal rather than immediately disabling protection.

Recommended Checks

  1. Delete the copy and download it again from the developer’s official site or the Mac App Store.
  2. Confirm that the app supports your macOS version and processor architecture.
  3. Compare the publisher’s checksum if one is provided.
  4. Inspect its Gatekeeper assessment and signature:
1
2

spctl --assess --verbose=4 /Applications/Example.app
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /Applications/Example.app
  1. If the trusted developer documents that the app is unsigned, Control-click it in Finder and choose Open, then review the more specific prompt. On current macOS versions, Privacy & Security may also show an Open Anyway choice for that one app.

Do not globally disable Gatekeeper with spctl --master-disable. Do not recursively remove quarantine metadata from unknown, cracked, or modified applications. Those approaches suppress the mechanism that is warning you and do not prove the application is safe. If a legitimate developer’s package fails verification, report it to the developer so they can provide a correctly signed and notarized build.

item.title: Run Legacy python 2.7 on macOS Safely with an Isolated Environment
item.description:
After a macOS upgrade, the system-provided python 2.7 interpreter was no longer available. That is expected on modern macOS releases.

python 2 reached end of life in 2020 and no longer receives security fixes. New development should use a supported python 3 release, and existing code should be migrated where possible.

If an old build process temporarily requires python 2.7, isolate it from the system rather than replacing macOS tools or making it the default python.
